title: Lemon & spinach chickpea skillet
description: A bright, one-pan meal with beans, greens, and a little lemon.
ingredients: 1 can (15 oz) chickpeas, drained and rinsed
instructions: Heat oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Cook onion for 5 minutes, stirring, until softened.
Add garlic and paprika; stir for 30 seconds. Add chickpeas and water; simmer for 5 minutes.
Stir in spinach a handful at a time and cook for 2–3 minutes until wilted.
Add lemon juice, salt if using, and pepper. Divide between two bowls; serve with toast or cooked rice if desired.
note: Serve with rice or toast. Chickpeas can be replaced with white beans.

title: Apple-cinnamon overnight oats
description: Breakfast that gets its work done while you sleep.
ingredients: ½ cup plain yogurt or plant-based yogurt
instructions: Mix oats, milk, yogurt, chia seeds, cinnamon, and optional syrup in a bowl.
Fold in apple and divide into two covered containers.
Refrigerate overnight, at least 8 hours. Stir before eating and add a splash of milk if needed.
note: 10 minutes of hands-on preparation plus overnight chilling. Choose certified gluten-free oats if needed; yogurt may contain milk or soy.

title: Black bean & pepper tacos
description: A quick taco night built around pantry beans and colorful peppers.
ingredients: 1 can (15 oz) black beans, drained and rinsed
instructions: Heat oil over medium heat in a skillet. Cook pepper and onion for 6–8 minutes until tender.
Add beans, cumin, paprika, and water. Simmer for 5 minutes, stirring; mash a few beans to thicken.
Warm tortillas in a dry skillet according to package directions.
Divide filling among tortillas and top with avocado and lime juice.
note: Add salsa if you like. Check tortilla labels when avoiding wheat.

title: Ginger tofu & broccoli rice bowls
description: Ginger, garlic, and a glossy sauce bring a simple bowl together.
ingredients: 1 block (14 oz) firm tofu, drained and patted dry
instructions: Cut dry tofu into ¾-inch cubes. Heat oil over medium-high heat in a large nonstick skillet.
Cook tofu for 8–10 minutes, turning gently, until browned on several sides.
Add broccoli and water, cover, and cook for 4–5 minutes until broccoli is tender.
Mix soy sauce, ginger, garlic, and maple syrup. Add to skillet and stir for 2 minutes; add a splash of water if too dry.
Serve over cooked rice.
note: Contains soy; regular soy sauce often contains wheat. Use labeled gluten-free tamari if needed. Time assumes rice is already cooked.

title: Tomato & white bean soup
description: A comforting pot of soup with pantry staples and room for your own seasoning.
ingredients: 2 cans (15 oz each) white beans, drained and rinsed
instructions: Heat oil over medium heat in a large pot. Cook onion and carrots for 7–8 minutes until softened.
Add garlic and oregano; stir for 30 seconds.
Add tomatoes, beans, and broth. Bring to a gentle boil, then simmer uncovered for 15 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Stir in spinach and cook for 2 minutes. Season with pepper; add water for a thinner soup.
note: Check broth labels for allergens. Serve with bread or a side salad.

title: Berry-banana breakfast cup
description: A no-cook breakfast with berries, creamy yogurt, and crunch.
ingredients: 1 cup plain yogurt or plant-based yogurt
instructions: Divide yogurt between two bowls or glasses.
Layer banana and berries over yogurt.
Add granola and pumpkin seeds just before eating to keep them crunchy.
note: Check yogurt and granola labels for milk, soy, nuts, and wheat. Use seed-free toppings if needed.

title: Lemon Salmon Bowl
description: Lemon, salmon and broccoli over quinoa for a simple dinner.
instructions: Heat oven to 400 F. Toss broccoli with 1 tsp oil; roast 10 min. Add salmon, brush with remaining oil and pepper; roast 10-15 min more, until fish reaches 145 F. Divide warm quinoa between bowls; add fish, broccoli and lemon juice.
note: Fish allergen. Use verified gluten-free ingredients and clean tools to prevent gluten cross-contact.

title: Chickpea Crunch Bowl
description: A fresh, no-cook bowl with chickpeas, cucumber and tomatoes.
ingredients: One 15-oz can no-salt-added chickpeas, drained and rinsed
instructions: Combine chickpeas, cucumber, tomatoes and parsley. Whisk oil, lemon juice and pepper. Toss together. Serve right away or chill until ready to eat.
note: For celiac disease: verify packaged ingredients are gluten-free; avoid cross-contact during preparation.
dietTags: Gluten-free with label checks and cross-contact precautions

title: Blueberry Overnight Oats
description: A make-ahead blueberry breakfast with oats, chia and soy milk.
instructions: Stir oats, soy milk, chia and cinnamon in a clean jar. Fold in half the berries. Cover and refrigerate overnight. Stir in the morning; top with remaining berries. Add a splash of soy milk if too thick.
note: Contains soy. *Use certified gluten-free oats. Some people with celiac disease cannot tolerate oats; follow your care plan. Preparation takes 5 minutes, plus overnight refrigeration.
dietTags: Certified gluten-free oats required; follow your celiac care plan
imageAlt: Blueberry Overnight Oats — illustrative food image

title: Cozy Lentil & Spinach Soup
description: A warming pot of lentils, carrots and spinach.
ingredients: 1 cup dry green lentils, rinsed and checked
instructions: Heat oil in a pot. Soften onion and carrots for 5 min; stir in cumin. Add lentils and broth. Bring to a boil; cover loosely and simmer 25-30 min, until tender. Add water if needed. Stir in spinach; cook 2 min.
note: For celiac disease: use labeled gluten-free broth and spices; prevent cross-contact. Lentils provide plant protein and fiber.
dietTags: Gluten-free with label checks and cross-contact precautions
imageAlt: Cozy Lentil & Spinach Soup — illustrative food image

title: Green & Gold Breakfast
description: Eggs and spinach with avocado and tomatoes for a colorful start.
instructions: Warm oil in a skillet; wilt spinach for 1 min. Beat eggs with pepper. Pour into pan and stir gently over medium-low heat until fully set and mixture reaches 160 F. Serve with avocado and tomatoes.
note: Contains egg. Gluten-free ingredients: verify labels and avoid cross-contact if preparing for celiac disease.
